sentences.text: Ask 1. The Chao family is searching on the internet and talking about things to do.
Listen to their discussion and write the information in the spaces below.
The first one has been provided as an example.
You now have 30 seconds to study the task.
At the end of the task you will have one minute to tidy up your answers.
So then let’s plan what to do today.
Any ideas? Let’s just go for a walk around the center of London.
But Dad, the center of London is really big and it’s too much walking.
Let’s do do something else.
Well, how about going to a museum?
London has lots of excellent museums according to this website your Dad is looking at.
Here are some exhibitions.
But museums are boring.
Can’t we do something more fun?
Not all museums are boring.
Have a look at this one, it’s the Video Games Museum.
Oh yes. That sounds interesting.
What kind of video games do they have?
Let’s have a look.
Oh, they have all kinds of video games, including a very early video game from 1958 called Tennis for Two.
Tennis for what?
Tennis for Two.
Oh yes, and there’s another one called Ping Pong from 1972.
I remember that one it’s like table tennis.
When is it from again?
That’s so old!
Are there any new games?
How about this one?
Teen Queen 4.
That’s from this year 2016!
And all my friends have Teen Queen 4!
Is there a Teen Queen 5?
No! Dad! Don’t be silly.
That’s for next year.
Shall we go then?
Sounds good to me.
Let’s have a look at the opening times.
Oh no, it’s closed on Wednesdays, so we can’t go today.
Oh! Well, it’s not the end of the world.
We can go another day.
Any other ideas?
What about this one?
The Railway Museum.
The Railway Museum?
Yes. That sounds boring.
Maybe not. It’s in an old station and you get to ride on an old train.
Actually that does sound boring.
Boring! No, it’s not boring and it’s quite cheap too.
It’s only two hundred and fifty Hong Kong Dollars per person.
two hundred fifty dollars per person!
That’s expensive! Yes, too expensive.
Plus it’s boring.
OK then, I guess you’re right.
Let’s look for this one?
The Museum of Youth Culture.
Youth culture? That sounds all right.
There’s an exhibition about toy ponies, one of your favourite toys.
You’ve still got your collection of toy ponies, haven’t you?
The My Pony Collection.
Yes, but I don’t play with my ponies very much now.
I’m a bit too old.
But you still like them?
Yeah, I suppose so.
Do you want to go see the exhibition of toy ponies?
Yes, OK. There’s also an exhibition about boy bands.
I don’t like boy bands anymore.
I thought you did.
Nope. How about this?
There’s an exhibition on children’s fashion.
That sounds boring.
No, but have a look at some of these pictures of the clothes.
Don’t they look interesting?
interesting? Oh yeah, those clothes look pretty cool!
I’d like to see that exhibition.
Finally! We’ve got a museum.
Let’s have a look at where the museum is.
Oh no, it’s quite far away Let’s have a look.
Oh, but it’s open late today.
OK, so we can go there later.
How much is it?
Oh look it’s free for school children on Wednesdays.
That means it’s free for Angela today.
Brilliant. And one more thing.
What? It’s interesting for all of us.
